evidence: backend/crates/db/src/repositories/llm_document.rs still exposes SIX public un-tenant-scoped methods that are the pre-remediation twins of the `_for_org` variants added for the cross-tenant IDOR fix (issue #766/#816): find_generation_request (:96, `SELECT * FROM llm_generation_requests WHERE id = $1`, no org filter), publish_description (:622, `UPDATE generated_listing_descriptions SET is_published = TRUE WHERE id = $1 RETURNING *`, no org filter), plus find_prompt_template (:336), find_listing_description (:531), update_edited_description (:594) and find_photo_enhancement (:1514). Their safe replacements sit right beside them (find_generation_request_for_org :113 and publish_description_for_org :640, both carrying `AND organization_id = $2` with the doc-comment 'a caller in org B cannot read/publish org A's ...').

The live routes were correctly migrated to the safe variants (backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/llm.rs:1442 calls find_generation_request_for_org, :1085 calls publish_description_for_org), and a grep across all of backend/ (excluding llm_document.rs itself and *_test.rs / tests/) returns ZERO non-test callers for all six un-scoped read/publish methods — so nothing is exploitable today. But the methods remain `pub` with a generic `E: Executor<'e, Database = Postgres>` bound, meaning a future caller can invoke them on the raw non-RLS `&state.db` pool (not an `acquire_with_rls(...)` guard), which reintroduces the exact cross-tenant read/mutate IDOR that #766/#816 closed — a latent security regression footgun. (Contrast update_generation_status at :205, also un-scoped `WHERE id = $1` but genuinely safe: its 3 live callers in llm.rs:619/669/975 all run on an org-context RlsPool guard where the Postgres RLS policy enforces isolation.)

Suggested fix: delete the six now-orphan un-scoped methods (they have no remaining callers), or, if an internal non-RLS use is still intended, gate them behind a narrower non-`pub` visibility / `#[doc(hidden)]` + rename (e.g. `*_unscoped_internal`) so a future route author cannot accidentally pick the IDOR-prone twin over the `_for_org` one. Cross-checked as net-new: no OPEN code-review-finding row currently tags segment=api-core, and the #766/#816 IDOR items in backlog.json cover the ROUTE-level fix, not this leftover-dead-repo-method footgun.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/regional_compliance.rs:341-361 (get_slovak_vote_minutes) and :893-916 (get_czech_usneseni) — both handlers generate an OFFICIAL LEGAL condominium voting-minutes document (Slovak 'zapisnica' under §14 z. 182/1993 Z.z. / Czech SVJ 'usneseni' under §1206 z. 89/2012 Sb.) but populate nearly every legally-material field with hardcoded placeholder constants instead of the actual vote's data.

Fabricated fields returned to the caller: meeting_date = NaiveDate 2024-01-15 (constant), meeting_location = 'Spolocenska miestnost, Hlavna 1, Bratislava' / 'Spolecenska mistnost, Hlavni 1, Praha' (constant), Czech svj_name = 'SVJ Hlavni 1' and ico = '12345678' (constant), total_ownership_shares = 10000, participating_shares = 7500, participation_percentage = 75.00, votes_for = 6000, votes_against = 1000, abstentions = 500, quorum_met = true, result_approved = true, participants = [] and questions = [] (empty). Only vote_id, building_id, title and the quorum_rule lookup reflect real data.

Impact: the endpoint emits a document that asserts a specific quorum was met and the motion was APPROVED with fabricated tallies (6000 for / 1000 against) for ANY vote id the caller can read — regardless of the vote's real outcome. This is a correctness/compliance defect on a legal artifact, not a cosmetic stub: a rejected or quorum-failed vote would still render as approved. Reachable in production (registered routes GET /api/v1/regional-compliance/slovak|czech vote minutes; vote lookup is RLS-scoped so the handler is live, only the body is fake).

Fix direction: derive meeting_date/location, ownership shares, participation, and the votes_for/against/abstentions tallies plus quorum_met/result_approved from the real poll + its cast votes (the same repo already loads the poll via vote_repo.find_poll_by_id_rls); do not hardcode the outcome. Same remediation applies verbatim to both the Slovak and Czech handlers.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/qrcode/QRCodeScanner.ts (385 lines, exports parseQRCode/getQRCodeAction/parsePPTPayload/parseVCard) and frontend/apps/mobile/src/qrcode/DeepLinkHandler.ts (292 lines, exports parseDeepLink/createDeepLink/DeepLinkManager) have NO dedicated test files anywhere in the repo — `find . -name 'QRCodeScanner.test.*'` and `DeepLinkHandler.test.*` both return zero hits. The only related tests are deepLinkRouting.test.ts / useDeepLinkRouting.test.tsx (the routing hook pipeline) and universalLinks.test.ts (the URL normalizer) — none exercise parseQRCode or parseDeepLink directly.

These are exactly the functions that ingest attacker-controllable input: parseQRCode(content: string) at QRCodeScanner.ts:29 dispatches raw scanned QR payloads across four parsers (ppt:// deep links, {"ppt":...} JSON, BEGIN:VCARD vCards, http(s) URLs) and getQRCodeAction routes the result to app navigation. A scanned QR code / opened deep link is untrusted external input, so a parsing bug here is a crash or mis-navigation path (e.g. an auth-required route reached via a crafted link), not a cosmetic issue.

Suggested fix: add unit tests covering malformed / adversarial inputs for parseQRCode (empty string, oversized payload, malformed JSON with "ppt": key, truncated vCard, ppt:// links to requiresAuth routes, javascript:/data: schemes) and parseDeepLink (unknown host, path traversal in :id params, extra query params). This is the highest-value untested surface in the segment.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/financial.tsx:70-135 — FinancialDashboardPageRoute issues three useQuery calls (getARAgingReport, getOverdueInvoices, listInvoices) but destructures ONLY `isLoading` from each (arLoading/overdueLoading/invoicesLoading); it never reads `isError`/`error`. FinancialDashboardPage (features/financial/pages/FinancialDashboardPage.tsx) has no `error` prop at all (props end at `isLoading?`).

On any query failure the fallbacks kick in silently: `totals = arReportData?.totals ?? {current:0,...,total:0}` (line ~87), `invoices = invoicesData?.invoices ?? []` (~95), `overdueInvoices = overdueData ?? []` (~96), and `isLoading` resolves to false. The dashboard then renders totalBalance=0, totalOutstanding=0, totalOverdue=0 and an empty invoice/overdue list — i.e. it presents FALSE '€0 / no overdue' financial data to a manager instead of an error state. Misleading zeroed data on a money path, not a cosmetic gap.

This is an inconsistency within the same file: the sibling FinancialReportsPageRoute at financial.tsx:437-438 already threads `error={activeQuery.error instanceof Error ? activeQuery.error.message : null}` into its child, so the correct pattern exists here and only the dashboard route omits it. Suggested fix: capture `isError`/`error` from the three dashboard queries, add an `error` prop to FinancialDashboardPage, and render an error/retry state instead of zeroed metrics when any query fails.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/financial/components/BudgetForm.tsx:127-128 — the editable Budget Categories list is rendered with `categories.map((category, index) => (<div key={index} ...>`, where each row holds two controlled inputs (category.name text input and category.amount number input).

The list is mutable: addCategory (BudgetForm.tsx:81) appends and removeCategory (:85) deletes with `setCategories(categories.filter((_, i) => i !== index))`, which re-indexes every subsequent element. Combined with `key={index}`, removing (or reordering) a non-last row makes React reconcile controlled inputs by position, so the deleted row's DOM/input state is reused for the following category — the classic index-key-on-editable-list bug: values appear to shift onto the wrong row, and in-progress edits/focus land on the wrong field after a mid-list delete.

Suggested fix: give each category a stable id at creation time (e.g. crypto.randomUUID() in addCategory and in the initial useState seed) and key the row by that id instead of the array index, keeping updateCategory/removeCategory index-based against the current array.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/imports.rs:120-132 — list_import_jobs (wired GET /api/v1/imports/jobs, PortalPrincipal-authenticated) forwards pagination straight to the repo with NO clamping: query.limit.unwrap_or(20) at :130 and query.offset.unwrap_or(0) at :131. ImportJobsQuery (imports.rs:90-94) types both as Option<i32>, so an attacker-supplied ?limit=2000000000 reaches the SQL LIMIT (unbounded result set / memory-amplification DoS) and ?offset=-1 reaches a Postgres OFFSET, which rejects negatives and surfaces as a 500.

This handler is the ONLY list endpoint in the reality-server routes that omits the clamp. Every sibling applies the exact guard it is missing: portal_listings.rs:431 `.clamp(1, 100)` + :432 `.max(0)`, reports.rs:290-291, agent_reviews.rs:85-86, realtors.rs:217-218, inquiries.rs:475/527, agencies.rs:124-125 `.clamp(1, 200)`, plus favorites.rs:275-279, saved_searches.rs:317-321 and articles.rs:355-359 which all do `.unwrap_or(DEFAULT).clamp(1, MAX)` on limit and `.max(0)` on offset. list_import_jobs is a straightforward oversight against an established, uniform repo convention.

Suggested fix: mirror the sibling handlers — `let limit = query.limit.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1, 100); let offset = query.offset.unwrap_or(0).max(0);` and pass the clamped values into list_import_jobs, so a hostile ?limit/?offset can neither exhaust memory nor trigger a negative-OFFSET 500.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/price_map.rs:97-131 — get_price_map is PUBLIC and unauthenticated (handler takes only State + Query, no principal). Its process-global cache PRICE_MAP_CACHE (static HashMap<String, CacheEntry>, price_map.rs:32-38) is keyed on `format!("{}:{}:{}:{}", mode, time_window, property_type, city)` at :125-131, where `city` (:53) and `property_type` (:55) are free-form, unvalidated user strings echoed straight into the key.

The only eviction is expiry-based: on each miss the write path does `cache.retain(|_, v| Instant::now() < v.expires_at)` (price_map.rs:236) then inserts an entry with a 1-hour TTL (:237-243, CACHE_TTL = 3600s at :41). There is NO size cap / LRU. Within any 1-hour window an attacker who varies `?city=` / `?property_type=` across unbounded distinct values inserts an unbounded number of live entries — retain never culls them because none have expired — giving a memory-exhaustion DoS on a public endpoint. Each distinct key is also a guaranteed cache miss, so every request additionally runs the heavy AVG(price/size_sqm) GROUP BY aggregation over the listings table (SQL at :158-213): a second, DB-amplification DoS axis.

Suggested fix: bound the cache (max entry count with LRU/random eviction, or an off-the-shelf bounded cache) AND validate `city`/`property_type` against the known set (or normalize/reject unknown values) before they become a cache key, so an unauthenticated caller cannot mint unbounded distinct keys or force unbounded uncached aggregations.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/regional_compliance.rs:253-259 (validate_slovak_vote, wired POST /api/v1/regional-compliance/slovak/voting/validate) and :799-805 (validate_czech_vote, wired POST /api/v1/regional-compliance/czech/svj/vote/validate) — the legal-validity endpoints fall back to a HARDCODED 75.00% participation (`Decimal::new(7500, 2)`) whenever `vote.eligible_count` resolves to 0 (`eligible_count.unwrap_or(0)` at :249-250 / :795-796). A vote whose eligible-voter count was never recorded (NULL/0) is therefore treated as having 75% turnout — a fabricated value, not derived from any real data.

Same handlers, :261-279 / :807-825 — `approval_percentage` defaults to a hardcoded 80.00% (`Decimal::new(8000, 2)`, and an inline `unwrap_or(80.0)`) whenever `vote.results` fails to deserialize into `VoteResults`, or has no questions, or the first question has no options. So an unparseable / empty results blob is scored as 80% approval.

Impact: `quorum_met = actual_participation >= required_quorum` and `is_valid = quorum_met && approval_percentage >= required_quorum` (:281-282) are computed FROM these fabricated defaults. With required_quorum <= 75/80% (simple_majority seeds 50.01%), a vote that has NO eligible-count and NO parseable results returns `quorum_met=true, is_valid=true` — a false 'legally valid' verdict emitted from placeholder numbers, on a production compliance endpoint. The validation_notes still assert 'Vote validation computed against seeded database jurisdiction rules', giving false assurance the tallies were real.

Contrast confirms it is a defect, not intent: the same handler already reads the REAL participation_count/eligible_count and parses vote.results when present, so the data path exists; the fallbacks silently substitute passing constants instead of surfacing INSUFFICIENT_DATA / 422. Fix direction: when eligible_count == 0 or results are unparseable/empty, return a determinate 'cannot validate — missing tally data' outcome (or is_valid=false with an explicit note) rather than defaulting to 75% / 80%. Applies verbatim to both the Slovak and Czech validators.

Distinct from the already-tracked `code-review-api-handlers-regional-compliance-fabricated-minutes` (2026-07-23) / `code-review-regional-compliance-hardcoded-vote-minutes` (2026-08-01): those cover the get_slovak_vote_minutes / get_czech_usneseni document builders returning all-constant bodies. THIS finding is the separate validate_* quorum/approval logic returning a fabricated PASS from fallback defaults.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useApi.ts:82-91 — the central `apiRequest` helper (backing every useQuery/useMutation in the app) reads the bearer token from SecureStore once (:66) and, on any non-ok response, just `throw new Error(message)` (:91). There is NO 401 branch, NO token-refresh attempt, and NO single-retry after refresh. A 401 from an expired access token is surfaced to the UI as a generic error identical to any other HTTP failure.

The recovery capability EXISTS but is never wired in: contexts/AuthContext.tsx defines `refreshToken()` (:209) that reads `ppt_refresh_token` from SecureStore and POSTs `/api/v1/auth/refresh` (:217-222). Grep across the whole app confirms `refreshToken()` is invoked ONLY from tests (test/integration/auth.integration.test.tsx:405,433,460) — never from production code. There is no `setInterval`/`setTimeout` proactive refresh and no 401 interceptor in AuthContext or useApi.

Impact: the backend uses short-lived access tokens with refresh-token rotation (docs/api/README.md). Once the access-token TTL lapses — which is guaranteed to happen in any normal session — every authenticated query and mutation fails with a spurious error, even though the client holds a valid refresh token that would transparently restore the session. The user is effectively soft-logged-out until they manually kill and re-login. Fix: in `apiRequest`, on a 401, call `AuthContext.refreshToken()` (or a shared refresh routine) once and retry the request; or add a proactive refresh timer keyed off the access-token `exp` claim (the code already decodes JWT claims via utils/jwt in getTenantId). Confidence medium: the missing-wiring is unambiguous from source; exact TTL-triggered timing is not runtime-confirmed.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCAccessController.ts:249-346 — `validateAccess` decides credential expiry (`new Date(credential.validUntil) < now`, :275) and time-of-day access windows (:299-336) entirely from device-local `new Date()` (:250, `now.getHours()`/`now.getDay()` :301-303). Device wall-clock is user-controllable; a holder of an expired or time-restricted credential can roll the phone clock back to make `validateAccess` return `granted: true`.

That client-side `granted` result is not merely advisory display: it GATES the physical transmit — `NativeNFC.transmitCredential(credential.encryptedData)` is only reached when `validationResult.granted` (NFCAccessController.ts:190-196). So clock tampering directly changes whether the credential is presented to the reader.

Impact: if the door reader / backend does NOT independently re-validate expiry and time-restrictions server-side, this is a physical-access bypass; if it does, this is still a defense-in-depth gap that lets revoked/expired credentials be transmitted. Fix: derive `now` from a trusted/monotonic or server-synced time source for the expiry + time-restriction checks (or make the reader authoritative and treat the client gate as UX-only). Confidence medium: exploitability depends on reader-side enforcement which is out of this segment's scope, but relying solely on device clock for credential expiry is a confirmed anti-pattern in the source.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCAccessController.ts (478 lines) and nfc/NFCCredentialManager.ts (321 lines) have ZERO test files — `find frontend/apps/mobile -name '*.test.*'` returns no nfc/ entry, and the covered-module list spans components/, config/, hooks/, navigation/, qrcode/, services/, utils/ and screens/{announcements,buildings,dashboard,documents,faults,forms,leases,messages,meters,neighbors,voting} but not nfc/.

These are the app's most security- and correctness-sensitive modules yet the non-trivial logic is untested: validateAccess's midnight-crossing time-window arithmetic (NFCAccessController.ts:318-321 `if (endMinutes < startMinutes) return currentMinutes >= startMinutes || currentMinutes <= endMinutes`), the status→denial-reason mapping (:256-262), and NFCCredentialManager's one-time SecureStore migration from the legacy AsyncStorage key with corrupt-data discard (NFCCredentialManager.ts:266-293).

Impact: a regression in the time-window or expiry logic silently grants or denies physical access with no failing test to catch it. Fix: add unit tests for validateAccess (each denial reason, expiry boundary, normal + midnight-crossing time windows) and for the credential-manager load/migrate/corrupt-discard paths. Low severity (test-coverage gap) but on a security-critical module.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/hooks/usePerformanceMetrics.ts:160-164 — the effect cleanup ONLY disconnects the PerformanceObservers (`for (const observer of observers) observer.disconnect()`). It never removes the two window event listeners the same effect registers: the `'load'` listener (`collectNavigationTiming`, :142) and, more importantly, the `'visibilitychange'` listener added at :153.

The `'visibilitychange'` handler at :153-157 is an inline anonymous arrow (`window.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (document.visibilityState === 'hidden') reportMetrics(); })`) — it has no stored reference, so it can NEVER be removed via removeEventListener even if a cleanup tried. `reportOnUnload` defaults to `true` (:45), so this listener is attached on every normal mount.

Effect deps are `[onReport, reportOnUnload]` (:165). A consumer that passes an inline/unstable `onReport` callback (the common React pattern) re-runs the effect on every render; each run stacks a brand-new anonymous `visibilitychange` listener on `window` that is never cleaned up. Over the lifetime of a long-lived SPA session this leaks listeners unboundedly, and every one of them fires `reportMetrics()` on each tab-hide — duplicating reports and holding closures over stale `metricsRef`/`onReport`.

Impact: memory / listener leak + duplicated metric reports on a hook that is intended to run app-wide (LCP/FID/CLS/TTFB web-vitals). Fix: store the visibilitychange handler in a named const and remove both it and the `'load'` listener in the cleanup return; and/or stabilise `onReport` with useCallback / a ref so the effect binds once. Note: distinct from the prior 2026-07-07 `perf-console-logs` finding (which was about dev console output in this same file), and not covered by any earlier ppt-web-core signal.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/ContentModerationPage.tsx:130-146 — free-form window.prompt() text is cast straight to a typed enum with no validation before being POSTed to the moderation API: `action_type: actionType as 'remove' | 'restrict' | 'warn' | 'approve'` (:143). A typo or unexpected casing ('Remove', 'ban', anything) passes the `if (!actionType) return` guard and is sent verbatim to takeAction.mutate — the union cast is a compile-time lie, TypeScript does not narrow it at runtime.

Same pattern at ContentModerationPage.tsx:169-181 — `decision: decision as 'uphold' | 'overturn'` from window.prompt for appeal decisions; and frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/AmlDashboardPage.tsx:143 — `decisionInput` window.prompt cast to the AML decision union ('approve','reject','escalate') then sent to review-assessment.

Impact: these are compliance / AML / content-moderation write paths (legally significant actions). An invalid enum reaches the backend and either 400s with a raw 'Failed to take action' alert (poor UX, no field-level feedback) or, if the backend is lenient, records a malformed action_type. The `as <union>` casts across the API boundary are exactly the unsafe-cast smell flagged for this segment. Fix: validate the prompt result against the allowed set (or replace window.prompt with a select/modal — already tracked as the Phase-2 TODO on the adjacent lines) before calling mutate.

Numerous user-facing browser-dialog strings are hardcoded English instead of going through react-i18next `t(...)`, even though the surrounding pages import and use useTranslation for other text.
